h1: The 8 Best Dehumidifiers Under $500 for Basements, Bedrooms and Whole Homes, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 dehumidifiers under $500 from 230 to 5500 sq ft, compared on pint capacity, tank size, drain hose and Energy Star rating.
summary: The AEOCKY 80 pint per day Energy Star dehumidifier is the one to buy under $500 if you need real whole-house capacity, with coverage listed up to 5500 square feet. The Kesnos 2000 sq ft unit adds a continuous drain hose and a timer for large rooms, and the TABYIK 101 oz tank is the high-capacity bundle with two closet boxes. The 95 oz units suit bedrooms.
intro: Dehumidifier shopping starts with a trick of language: coverage claims. A unit that says 1000 square feet and a unit that says 5500 square feet are not different sizes of the same machine, they may be different technologies. Compressor machines rated in pints per day can pull gallons from a damp basement, while small tank-based units with a coverage number but no pint rating are built for a bedroom. The rating that matters is pints per day under stated conditions.

We reviewed eight dehumidifiers from their listings, from a 230 sq ft compact unit to an 80 pint per day Energy Star machine, ranking them by stated capacity, coverage, drain options, safety features and price. Several listings give no pint rating at all, and we flag those gaps. Price buckets replace exact prices, and nothing here comes from test results.

products.name: AEOCKY 5500 Sq.Ft Energy Star Most Efficient 2025 Dehumidifier Max 80Pint/D
products.verdict: An Energy Star certified machine with an 80 pint per day maximum and 5500 square foot coverage.
products.description:
The AEOCKY is a full-size dehumidifier with a listed 5500 square foot coverage, an 80 pint per day maximum capacity and Energy Star certification, in the $200 to $500 range.

It wins because it is the only machine here that matches the numbers on its label. A pint-per-day rating is the industry measure of how much water a dehumidifier removes, and 80 pints is a large-capacity class meant for damp basements and whole-floor use. Energy Star certification means a verified efficiency standard, which counts because a dehumidifier runs for hours. The cost is size and weight, and a price near the top of this guide.

Buy it if you need to dry a basement, a crawl space or a large open floor. Skip it if you only have a damp closet.
products.idealFor: Basements, crawl spaces and large floors.
products.skipIf: You only need a closet or bedroom unit.

products.name: Kesnos 34 Pin Dehumidifiers for Home and Basements, Dehumidifiers For
products.verdict: A 2000 sq ft unit with a continuous drain hose, 24-hour timer, child lock and auto defrost.
products.description:
The Kesnos is listed for homes and basements, with a 2000 sq ft coverage, a continuous drain hose, a 24-hour timer, a child lock and auto defrost. The name suggests a 34-pint class rating.

The drain hose is the feature that changes daily life. A tank must be emptied by hand, often twice a day in a damp basement, but a hose runs the water to a floor drain or a sump and removes the chore. Auto defrost lets the unit keep working in cooler rooms, where coils otherwise ice up, and the timer lets you run it off-peak. It ranks second because its capacity is lower than the AEOCKY's, and the listing's title is cut off.

Buy it if you have a large room or a basement with a drain. Skip it if you need whole-house capacity.

products.name: TABYIK Dehumidifiers for Home, 101oz Dehumidifier & 2pack Rechargeable
products.verdict: A 101 oz tank unit sold with two rechargeable dehumidifying boxes for closets.
products.description:
The TABYIK bundles a dehumidifier with a 101 oz tank and a two-pack of rechargeable dehumidifying boxes. The 101 oz tank is the largest tank in this ranking.

The bundle is a clever idea for a household with several damp spots: the main unit handles a bedroom or living space, and the rechargeable boxes sit in closets and cabinets where a machine will not fit. Rechargeable boxes absorb moisture and then dry out on a charger. The listing gives no coverage or pint rating, so you cannot judge how large a space the main unit handles.

Buy it if you want to treat a room and several small enclosed spaces at once. Skip it if you want a stated capacity.
products.idealFor: Homes with a room and several closets.
products.skipIf: You want a stated coverage area.

products.name: KeepGlad Dehumidifier, 98OZ Dehumidifiers for Home(1000sq.ft), Humidity
products.verdict: A 98 oz tank and 1000 sq ft listed coverage for a standard room, at $50 to $100.
products.description:
The KeepGlad lists a 98 oz tank and 1000 square feet of coverage, and costs between $50 and $100. It is the straightforward room-sized unit in the group.

A 98 oz tank holds roughly three quarters of a gallon, which is a useful buffer in a damp room, though it will fill fast in a very humid one. The 1000 sq ft figure is a seller claim, and a unit without a pint rating is better judged by the room's real conditions. It ranks fourth because the listing offers no extras such as a drain hose or a timer.

Buy it if you want a no-frills unit for a bedroom, office or small living room. Skip it if you want a drain hose or a sleep mode.
cons: No drain hose or timer listed
products.idealFor: Bedrooms, offices and small living rooms.

products.name: ToLife Dehumidifier, 1000 Sq Ft 95 oz Tank with Sleep Mode, Auto Shutoff
products.verdict: A 95 oz tank, 1000 sq ft coverage, a sleep mode and an auto shut-off for bedrooms.
products.description:
The ToLife lists a 95 oz tank, 1000 sq ft coverage, a sleep mode and an auto shut-off, at $50 to $100.

A sleep mode is the reason to pick it over the KeepGlad. Bedrooms are where noise and lights hurt, and a mode that lowers fan speed or dims indicators lets you run the unit overnight. Auto shut-off stops the machine when the tank fills, which protects the floor. It ranks fifth because its core numbers are nearly the same as the KeepGlad's, and the price is the same.

Buy it if the unit will live in a bedroom. Skip it if you want a drain hose for a basement.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms where noise and light matter.

products.name: NineSky Dehumidifiers for Home, 1000 Sq.Ft Dehumidifier with 95oz Water
products.verdict: A 95 oz tank and 1000 sq ft coverage with a 7-color ambient light.
products.description:
The NineSky lists a 95 oz water tank, 1000 sq ft coverage and a 7-color ambient light, at $50 to $100.

The ambient light is a style feature, a soft glow that works as a night light in a nursery or a living room. It adds nothing to drying, and some sleepers dislike light in the bedroom, so check that it can be switched off. The core specs match its cousins, so the choice between this one and the ToLife comes down to taste.

Buy it if you like the lighting and want a room-sized unit. Skip it if you want features that help drying.
products.idealFor: Rooms where a soft glow is welcome.
products.skipIf: You sleep badly with any light on.

products.name: BEDRED Dehumidifier, 95OZ Dehumidifier for Home 1000 sq ft - Quiet with
products.verdict: A 95 oz, 1000 sq ft dehumidifier marketed as quiet, with a truncated listing.
products.description:
The BEDRED lists a 95 oz tank, 1000 sq ft coverage and quiet operation, at $50 to $100. The title is cut off, so the full feature list is unclear.

It ranks seventh because the listing here shows only the headline numbers. An earlier compact BEDRED listing named semiconductor thermoelectric cooling, which is quiet but weaker in cool rooms, and that is worth asking the seller about before relying on a 1000 sq ft claim. Quiet running makes it a fit for a bedroom or office.

Buy it if silence matters and the room is warm. Check the cooling type and removal rate first.
products.skipIf: The room is cool or very damp.

products.name: Dehumidifier 1657ML 58OZ Small Dehumidifier for Home 230 Ft² Safety
products.verdict: A compact 58 oz, 230 sq ft unit with safety features, for the lowest cost.
products.description:
This compact dehumidifier lists a 1657mL (58 oz) tank, 230 square feet of coverage and safety protection, at $25 to $50.

It is here as the budget end of the range, and it is the only unit with a modest, honest coverage figure. A 230 sq ft claim suits a small bedroom or an office, and that is the right scale for a unit this size. It ranks last in a guide with a $500 ceiling because it cannot treat a basement or a large room.

Buy it if you have a single small room and want the lowest cost. Step up to the Kesnos or KeepGlad for anything bigger.
products.idealFor: A single small bedroom or office.
products.skipIf: You have a basement or large room.

whatMatters.detail: The pint rating states how much water a unit can remove in 24 hours at set conditions. Larger numbers suit damper, bigger spaces. A listing with coverage but no pint rating tells you much less, so treat unsupported coverage claims with care.
Coverage is a rough guide, not a guarantee. A 1000 sq ft claim assumes moderate dampness. In a wet basement, you need a unit rated well above the room size. When unsure, pick the next size up.

A tank must be emptied by hand, while a continuous drain hose sends water to a floor drain or sump. In a basement, a hose is a major convenience. Look for continuous drain in the listing, as on the Kesnos.
Cool rooms can freeze the coils of a compressor unit. Auto defrost clears the ice and keeps the machine working. If you will use the dehumidifier in an unheated space, this feature matters.

A dehumidifier runs for hours, so efficiency adds up. Energy Star certification, as on the AEOCKY, signals a verified efficiency standard. It lowers running cost without changing how well the machine dries.

faq.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for a basement?
faq.a: It depends on dampness and area, but a basement usually needs a pint-rated compressor machine, such as an 80 pint model for large or wet spaces. Units with only a tank size and coverage claim are better for bedrooms.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a dehumidifier?
faq.a: Buying on the coverage number alone. Without a pint-per-day rating, a coverage figure means little. Check the capacity, then check the drain method.

faq.q: Is the AEOCKY worth it over a 95 oz unit?
faq.a: For a basement or large floor, yes. The 80 pint rating and Energy Star certification are on a different scale from a 95 oz tank unit. For a bedroom, the cheaper unit is the sensible choice.
Place the unit on a flat surface with space around the vents, plug it in, set your target humidity and close the room. For a drain hose, attach it and run it downhill to a drain.

faq.q: What humidity should I aim for?
faq.a: Many sources suggest keeping indoor humidity around 30 to 50 percent. A humidity meter shows your actual level. Too low can cause dry skin and static, so use the dehumidifier's humidity setting.

faq.q: How do I clean a dehumidifier?
faq.a: Empty and rinse the tank regularly, wipe the filter and let parts dry. Standing water breeds odors and mold. Check the manual for filter cleaning intervals.

finalTake: For a basement or whole floor, the AEOCKY 80 pint Energy Star dehumidifier is the best buy under $500, and the Kesnos is the better fit when you have a floor drain. The TABYIK bundle adds closet boxes, and the ToLife suits bedrooms with its sleep mode. Compare pint ratings first, because coverage claims alone can mislead.
